h1: Chaisuk Bungalow — Clean Garden Bungalows at Hundreds-of-Baht Rates Near the Khlong Luek Border
intro: If you're planning to cross the Khlong Luek border into Cambodia, or to hit Rong Kluea Market early, and you want an easy, cheap place to sleep for one night — Chaisuk Bungalow is a pick that budget travellers and cyclists mention often. It's a bungalow-style stay set in a garden, with clean rooms, cold air-con and free parking, in Aranyaprathet town about 5 km from the border and walkable to the railway station. Rooms start at around THB 300/night — ideal if you want a clean place to sleep at great value rather than a stay with full facilities.

body.html: Chaisuk Bungalow sits at 23/1 Suwannason Road, Km.2, Aranyaprathet Sub-district — a budget stay in town, about 5 km from the Khlong Luek border crossing and Rong Kluea Market, and roughly a 20-minute walk from Aranyaprathet railway station. It's a bungalow-style property with rooms spread across a garden rather than a tower block, so it's quieter and leafier than a typical in-town hotel. The pitch is simple: clean rooms at a low price for travellers stopping over before crossing the border or shopping the market.

What guests mention most is that the rooms are cleaner than the price suggests, and the bungalows are bigger than expected. Many reviews say the rooms really are clean, with fresh linens, cold air-con and decent hot-water pressure. Some rooms are large bungalows with a seating area and a garden outlook, and a few have a fridge. There's a range from Economy rooms to larger double bungalows, with the rate rising by size and amenities. Self-drivers and cyclists often say a clean air-con room for a few hundred baht is excellent value for a one-night stop.
"The bungalow was bigger than expected, the room was very clean and the air-con was cold — paying a few hundred baht for an air-con room like this is great value for an overnight before the border."

For self-drivers and cyclists, the advantages here are free private parking on site and a location close to the Khlong Luek border, Rong Kluea Market and the railway station. You can walk out to restaurants and convenience stores nearby, and the garden setting is quiet enough for a good night's sleep away from main-road noise. It's well suited to arriving late and getting up early to queue at the border, or to reach Rong Kluea Market when it opens and the stalls are full and uncrowded.

To be honest — this is a genuine budget stay: no breakfast, no pool, and the staff speak limited English, so foreign travellers may want a translation app on hand. Bathrooms and amenities are basic, some rooms have few power outlets, and a few bungalows show wear or maintenance niggles in line with the property's age. Travellers after design, a cafe or full facilities may find it too plain and basic for their taste.

In short, Chaisuk Bungalow suits anyone wanting a clean air-con room in a garden setting, at a few hundred baht, for a one-night stop before crossing the Khlong Luek border into Cambodia or shopping Rong Kluea Market early. The overall score of around 8.0 from real reviews, and its standing as a top specialty-lodging pick in Aranyaprathet on TripAdvisor, reflect exactly what it is — clean, good value, well placed. Just understand you're buying a "clean, cheap bedroom", not a "resort experience". Set expectations accordingly and this is one of the most dependable budget picks near the border.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Chaisuk Bungalow Aranyaprathet

faq.q: Where is Chaisuk Bungalow located in Aranyaprathet?
faq.a: It's at 23/1 Suwannason Road, Km.2, Aranyaprathet Sub-district, in town. It's about 5 km from the Khlong Luek border crossing and Rong Kluea Market, and roughly a 20-minute walk from Aranyaprathet railway station — a handy base for an overnight before the border or an early market run.

faq.q: What's the starting price and what rooms are available?
faq.a: Rates start at around THB 300/night for an Economy Double, with a Superior Double around THB 400 and a Large Double/Twin bungalow around THB 500. Prices rise by room size and season — book ahead and compare platforms for the best rate.

faq.q: What are the rooms like — are they clean?
faq.a: The strength here is rooms cleaner than the price suggests, with bungalows bigger than expected. They have air-con, TV, en-suite bathroom and decent hot water, with a fridge in some rooms. Bathrooms and amenities are basic and some rooms have few outlets, but overall they're clean and good value for a budget stay.

faq.q: Is there breakfast and a pool?
faq.a: There's no breakfast service and no pool here — it's a budget stay focused on clean, well-priced rooms. For breakfast, plan a spot in Aranyaprathet town or stop at a nearby convenience store before you set off.

faq.q: Is there parking — is it good for border crossings?
faq.a: Yes — there's free private parking on site. The location near the Khlong Luek border, Rong Kluea Market and the railway station makes it ideal for self-drivers and cyclists wanting an overnight before crossing into Cambodia or shopping Rong Kluea Market early.

faq.q: Who is this hotel best for?
faq.a: It's best for anyone wanting a clean air-con room in a garden setting, at a few hundred baht, for a one-night stop before the Khlong Luek crossing or a Rong Kluea Market run. It's less suited to travellers after design, a pool, or breakfast at the hotel.
